prompt: Why did trial signups drop 18% last week?

chunks.content:
>> [E1] H0: dashboard vs backend gap by channel and device (14 rows)
>> [E2] H1: ad platform changes during the two weeks (2 rows)
Verdict: H2 SUPPORTED — E1 shows the dashboard/backend gap widened by ~184 signups last week, concentrated almost entirely on mobile (organic −59, paid_search −47, direct −31, paid_social −24, email −18; desktop gaps near zero), a mobile tracking/event-capture artifact explaining ~47% of the 389-signup dashboard drop. H1 SUPPORTED (partial) — E2 shows campaign 101 daily budget cut 1200→500 on 2026-10-13 and campaign 201 creative changed on 2026-10-14; paid search dashboard fell 609→419 (−190), but part of that is the mobile measurement gap, so the true ad-driven effect needs spend data to size.

REMAINING: H3 pricing; H4 holidays/seasonality; H5 real demand (non-paid residual).
DECISIONS: Dashboard = trial_signups_daily; backend = accounts; measurement gap ≈184 (~47% of 389 drop), real decline ≈104 (~53%).

>> [E6] H5: backend trial signups by channel and device prior vs last week to isolate non-paid real demand residual (14 rows)
Verdict: H5 real demand is SUPPORTED (small). Backend non-paid signups fell 37 total — organic −37, referral −10, direct +9, email +1 [E6] — confirming modest real demand softness outside paid channels. Paid search accounts fell 158 (desktop −105, mobile −53) [E6], consistent with the H1 ad-spend cut [E2,E3]; paid social −9 and display −1 [E6] sum to the −205 backend decline [E6]. Against the −389 dashboard drop [E1], the ≈184 dashboard–backend gap is measurement, not business change [E1]; paid search explains ≈158; residual non-paid real demand ≈37; paid social/display ≈10. These components sum to the full drop, leaving no material unexplained residual.
